description: Test your ability to predict async execution order, promise chains, async/await behavior, error handling, and parallel task patterns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt:
What does this code log?
```js
Promise.resolve(2)
  .then((number) => number * 2)
  .then((number) => console.log(number));
```
questions.explanation: The first `.then()` returns `4`, which becomes the value for the next `.then()`.
Throwing inside `.then()` rejects the chain, and `.catch()` handles it.

options.text: If `loadUser()` returns a rejecting Promise, this catch will not catch it unless the promise is awaited
`try...catch` cannot be used in async code at all

questions.explanation: Promise rejections must be handled with `.catch()` or `await` inside `try...catch`.

questions.prompt: Which version runs independent tasks in parallel?

options.text: `const a = await taskA(); const b = await taskB();`

questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` starts both promises and waits for both results.

questions.prompt: What order are `Promise.all()` results returned in?
questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` results match the order of the input promises, even if completion order differs.

questions.prompt: Which API waits for all promises even if some reject?
questions.explanation: `Promise.allSettled()` returns results for both fulfilled and rejected promises.

options.text: `forEach` does not wait for promises returned by async callbacks

questions.explanation: Use `for...of` for sequential waits or `Promise.all(users.map(...))` for parallel waits.

questions.prompt: When is sequential `await` the right choice?

options.text: When each step depends on the result of the previous step
Only when there are no promises
Never; sequential await is always wrong

questions.explanation: Sequential await is correct when later work needs earlier results or order matters.

questions.prompt: What is a good use for promise `.finally()` or `finally` with async/await?

options.text: Cleanup such as turning off loading state

questions.explanation: `finally` is useful for cleanup that should happen on success or failure.
